title: Dominated convergence in $L^p$
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $E$ be a normed additive group, and let $p$ be a nonzero finite extended nonnegative real number. Suppose $(F_k)_{k\in\mathbb N}$ consists of functions $\Omega\to E$ that are strongly measurable almost everywhere, and that a real-valued function $b$ belongs to $L^p(\mu)$. If $\|F_k(x)\|\le |b(x)|$ for almost every $x$ for each $k$, and $F_k(x)\to0$ for almost every $x$, then $\|F_k\|_{L^p(\mu)}\to0$.
hypotheses_covered: Each $F_k$ is strongly measurable almost everywhere
